summary: Intermittent GPU eviction spikes in dedicated pool causing increased tail latency and 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden increases in inference latency and sporadic 504 Gateway Timeouts for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool. Impacts multiple routes and model versions.

Impact:
- Elevated 99th and 99.9th percentile latencies (generating >2s extra tail latency).
- Intermittent 504s observed for ~5-10% of requests during spike windows.
- Customer traffic is on a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) and expects steady throughput.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: cw-dedicated-usw-3
- Region: us-west
- Models: redwood-13b-v1.2 (primary), rw-lite-7b-v0 (fallback)
- Time windows: first observed 2026-03-12 22:30 UTC, recurring 2026-03-13 01:10-02:00 UTC and 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer traffic pattern):
1) Heavy sustained multi-tenant training-like bursts from internal tenant in same pool (not CloudWave).
2) Prefix-heavy requests with long prompt lengths (avg seq len ~1k tokens) spike KV cache and GPU memory usage.
3) Serving runtime shows increased queueing and occasional worker process OOM or eviction.

Observed logs/metrics (excerpt):
- kubelet evictions increase: kube_events.eviction.count spikes coincident with tail-latency windows.
- Node GPU memory saturation: nvidia_smi shows 98-100% memory used on impacted nodes for short intervals.
- Serving runtime traces: worker_restarts and cache_evictions metrics increase.
- Autoscaler show undershoot: desired_replicas=8, available_replicas=5 during the window.

Initial customer impact statement:
"We are seeing timeouts across a subset of calls — this started after last week's model rollout. Our SLAs are being violated and we need mitigation to restore baseline throughput."
investigation_notes:
2026-03-13 03:00 Miguel: Pulled node-level metrics and kube events. Evidence of transient GPU memory pressure followed by container restarts on 3 of 12 nodes in pool cw-dedicated-usw-3. Eviction traces correlate with noisy tenant allocations.
2026-03-13 07:20 SRE (Lin): Autoscaler logs show scaling attempts failing because new nodes failed readiness checks due to driver mismatch on one host (AMI drift). Bootstrap failures caused desired capacity to be unmet.
2026-03-13 09:05 Support (Asha): Captured serving-runtime logs (link: https://logs.redwood.ai/goto/SUP-31845) showing LRU cache thrash and continuous KV cache reallocations. Hypothesis: combination of noisy neighbor memory footprint + autoscaler undershoot during bursts triggering head-of-line queuing and occasional worker OOM.
2026-03-13 11:40 Eng (Priya): Checked GPU isolation metrics — multi-tenant scheduling allowed a high-memory batch job (non-LLM) to run on same node set due to relaxed node taints. That job consumed a large fraction of GPU memory for 1-3 minute windows.

Key findings so far:
- Root cause is multi-factor: noisy tenant heavy-memory jobs + autoscaler failing to meet desired capacity fast enough (bootstrap/readiness errors) + relaxed GPU isolation/taints allowing co-location.
- This results in transient high GPU memory occupancy, triggering process restarts/evictions and increased request queuing leading to 504s.

Corroborating links:
- Grafana dashboard (tail latency): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tail/SUP-31845
- Node events snapshot: https://k8s.redwood.ai/evictions/cw-dedicated-usw-3/2026-03-13
comments: 2026-03-13 - CloudWave Support (J. Lee): We started seeing 504s around 22:30 UTC last night. Request IDs: r_3f1b9d, r_aad12f. Can you check if any model changes were pushed?

2026-03-13 - Asha Patel (Support): Thank you — no model rollout to the customer's pool from Redwood occurred at that window. Opening investigation with SRE to check pool health. Assigned to Miguel Torres.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Initial triage: observed node-level evictions and nvidia-smi memory saturation on a subset of nodes. Collecting full traces and autoscaler logs. Will attempt to isolate noisy tenant and throttle or cordon nodes if necessary.

2026-03-13 - Lin (Infra): Autoscaler logs show 3 bootstrap failures (AMI driver mismatch). Raising INT ticket to patch base image and re-run node bootstrap. Temporary mitigation: manually bring up 3 replacement nodes with correct image.

2026-03-13 - Priya (Platform Eng): Found a batch job from tenant tenant-47 scheduled without GPU taint control. Suggest enforce stricter nodeSelector/taint for high-memory jobs in dedicated pools. Preparing policy PR.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Temporary workaround implemented at 2026-03-13T12:30Z: cordoned two noisy nodes and scaled pool min_replicas to 10 to prevent undershoot. Observed tail latency dropped to near baseline within 8 minutes. Monitoring ongoing.

2026-03-14 - CloudWave Support (J. Lee): Thanks for the quick mitigation — we still saw a single 504 at 2026-03-14 02:10 UTC but overall throughput looks better. Please confirm permanent fixes and next steps.

2026-03-14 - Asha Patel (Support): We're coordinating a permanent mitigation: patch autoscaler bootstrap, enforce taints for batch workloads, and add an autoscaler cooldown policy. Planning follow-up change window with customer for 2026-03-18.
2026-03-14 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Created INT-4089 to track autoscaler image drift remediation and INT-4090 to enforce node taint policies. Will monitor for 48 hours post-change window.
resolution:
Workarounds applied: cordoned noisy nodes, temporarily increased min_replicas to avoid undershoot during bursts, and routed a small percentage of traffic to rw-lite-7b-v0 fallback to reduce memory pressure.
Planned permanent actions:
- INT-4089: Fix autoscaler bootstrap image mismatch and add health checks to avoid readiness flaps.
- INT-4090: Add scheduling guards/taints to prevent colocating high-memory batch jobs with low-latency inference workers in dedicated pools.
- PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5123 to instrument eviction metrics and improved alerting.
Follow-up: Change window scheduled 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC (customer-approved) to roll pool nodes and apply the autoscaler patch. Target: full mitigation and close after 48h monitoring with no regressions.
next_steps:
- Execute INT-4089 and INT-4090 during the approved change window.
- Monitor 99/99.9 latency and eviction metrics for 48h post-deploy.
- Update customer with post-change report and close ticket if stable.
- Create a postmortem if similar events reoccur after fixes.
notes: This ticket overlaps thematically with prior tickets SUP-9271 and SUP-21456 but differs in root cause: here autoscaler bootstrap failures + scheduling policy gaps allowed a noisy tenant to co-locate, amplifying memory pressure. Recommend tagging dedicated pools with stricter scheduling policies going forward.
